newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minibudget cuts seen 15-16 trln lire - cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Italy minibudget cuts seen 15-16 trln lire - cabinet.

text.p: The Italian government will unveil a mini-budget before the end of the month which will include 15-16 trillion lire ($8.9-$9.5 billion) of deficit cutting measures, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said on Friday.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has pledged to do everything needed to ensure that the public deficit is cut to three percent of gross domestic product this year to guarantee Italy a place among the founder members of the single European currency.

Micheli told reporters after a cabinet meeting that all options remained open over the content of the budget package. Among measures widely expected are a transfer of company severence payment funds to Treasury coffers and a one-off tax on people who have taken early retirement.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi presented the cabinet with details of eagerly awaited first quarter accounts. Micheli said they pointed to the economy growing between 1.2-1.4 percent this year after a 0.8 percent increase in 1996.
The government originally forecast GDP growth of two percent for 1997. The Bank of Italy said last month that 1997 growth would be little different from that seen in 1996.

The new data means that without additional budget action, the deficit/GDP ratio would be 3.8 percent this year. The Maastricht Treaty demands that countries wishing to sign up to European economic and monetary union should have a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent.
